title: Variational inference via Wasserstein gradient flows
tldr_zh: Gaussian VI 即 KL 在 Bures-Wasserstein 子流形上的梯度流（Särkkä ODE），强 log-concave 下有 e^{-2αt} 与 SGD 非渐近界
tldr_en: Gaussian VI is the KL gradient flow on the Bures-Wasserstein manifold (Särkkä's ODE); strongly log-concave targets give exponential rates and a non-asymptotic SGD bound; mixtures become interacting Gaussian particles.
key_numbers: Continuous time: W2^2(p_t, pi_hat) <= exp(-2 alpha t) W2^2(p_0, pi_hat) when Hessian V >= alpha I > 0 (Corollary 3)
BW-SGD: E W2^2(p_k, pi_hat) <= exp(-alpha k h) W2^2(p_0, pi_hat) + 36 d h / alpha^2 for h <= alpha^2/60; eps^2 accuracy with k >~ d/(alpha^3 eps^2) log(W2(p_0,pi_hat)/eps) (Theorem 4)
Stationarity of Gaussian VI: E_pi_hat grad V = 0, E_pi_hat Hess V = Sigma_hat^{-1} (Eq. 7)
Experiments: logistic-regression posterior in d=2 and d=100, KL below Laplace approximation (Fig. 2, curves only); 40 Gaussian particles fit a GMM target (Fig. 3, qualitative)
Mixture-of-Gaussians KL objective is non-convex on P2(BW) even for strongly log-concave pi (Appendix G)
